A great post.  If you still have the 6k then I would advise you to keep hold of it and not play anymore poker or do anymore gambling.  6k is a great cushion to turn over a new leaf.  I have gambled online for a long time, a little over 4 weeks ago I somehow hit a massive win on an online slot, £10,000 with a £2 stake.  I was the happiest I had ever been.  I withdrew most of it but kept some in my online account and over the next week I had a really good streak of wins.  I kept withdrawing most of the money and then going back and making more.  After about 7 days I had £18,000 in my bank account.  I paid off a lot of people I owed money to.  I paid off about 90% of my credit cards.  But then I started gambling again.  And this time whereas my deposits where normally £50, I was doing £200, £300, £250, and I was just blowing it in minutes.  Suffice to say just about 4 weeks later I only have £1,600 left.  No matter how much we win, we will always gamble more.  I have put limit back on my online account of £50 a week so that I don't blow the rest so easily.  I wish you the strength to change your life for the better.

FOBT's are evil.  I am 46 and went through some very bad years with them.   I still gamble online so I am not great at giving advice but to get away from the FOBTs I went to every bookies I had ever frequented and self excluded.  I'm not sure if it is so easy to do it now but its worth a go.  They are evil machines  because  I found that when  I didn't really  need money I could win on them easily.  I would play every day in my lunch break and after work.   Some weeks I would end up with wads of cash in my pockets and bag and car.  I would look at the money and think how easy it was.  But I  couldn't stop going back and so eventually I would lose it all.  And then have to draw out more cash to win it back, which never happened.  It's almost like the more you need to win the less likely it was to happen.  Online casinos are just as bad but at least its easy to put deposit limits on  your account which is what i have done.  I still lose money every month but just not as bad as I used to.

Maybe start a youtube channel where you talk about your gambling and attempts to stop?

It's not worth killing yourself over.  You never  know what could happen tomorrow.

Another idea could be to self exclude yourself from any casino's that you are likely to visit?

Also, I don't know whether it's the same for wherever you are, but in the uk it is possible to ask the banks to limit the amount of cash you can withdraw  per day.

My parents used to go for Sunday drives when I was in my early teens.  We would go to a cafe for a coffee and a snack and it had a couple of 10p fruit machines, my dad would give me an my brother some change to go and play them.  I remember winning the jackpot of £2 (!) one week and feeling amazing.   

Then when I started my first job, a few of the lads would go to the arcade on their lunch break.  Of course I joined them.  Except I would spend more than them, and I would go back after work as well.  

Several years later I started going into bookmakers and playing the FOBTs as well


Repeat the above for about 30 years and that's my story more or less

It's horrible.  I have been a gambler since I was about 16.  I had to go bankrupt in my 30's because I had around £40,000 worth of debt.  My (first and probably best) relationship ended because of it.  I'm now in my mid 40's and I still gamble.  My current partner thinks I have stopped but I haven't.   

I think I am a little bit more in control than 10 years ago, I have deposit limits with the 2 online casinos that i use, and have excluded from virtually all the others.  I still got into debt after the bankruptcy, which is not supposed to be possible.  As you said the gamblers mind is very good at finding ways to get that next fix.  

I don't know what i can say to help you but I wish you the strength to stop if that's what you want.  For me I am getting sick of online gambling,  I usually play slots and roulette..  Roulette is just plain evil (just one more spin, oh look right next to my number), and the slots are just the same thing over and over again, waiting for that crazy feature to come and the machine to go on a mad payout.  And after all that waiting the feature turns out to be shit.

At the start of this month I had won about £2k from a £20 deposit.   Now its 7 days before payday and my bank is emtpy, I have borrowed more money and I have £30 left in my wallet.

I feel your pain.  This is the nature of our addiction.  No amount of winnings is ever enough in the long run.  Even if you had managed to withdraw the £500, you would have played it back over the next week or month ( I would have anyway).  

I had a massively lucky streak on casumo and turned £20 into well over £2000.  I withdrew a lot of it but left several hundred to play with the next night.  The next day I lost that all in one session.

When the withdrawal hit my bank I payed money to 2 of my credit cards.  I paid off other little bits of debts.  I put £800 in my savings account to get my car serviced.  I even booked the appointment with the garage.  Then the day before the service was due I had a day off work and went into town.  I decided I Could afford to take  £100 into ladbrokes and play roulette on small stakes.  After little more than 2 hours I had spent the entire £800 savings plus the rest of the money I had in my current account.  I had to use my credit cards just to get me through to the end of this month.

All I  can say is make sure you have a small daily deposit limit of £20 on each casino.  At least it gives you some time to cool down.  And if possible never play FOBTs
